title: Atomic state cutover validation and graceful degradation protocol
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: define and validate an active-passive cutover that guarantees atomic state promotion for latency-sensitive services while providing deterministic graceful degradation and load-shedding behavior. This ticket covers the playbook for promotion, verification of backup/restore integrity (KV and tokenstore), circuit-breaker profiling to avoid cascading failures during partial capacity, and a scheduled drill plan for a full passive-to-active rehearsal.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Playbook fully documented with step-by-step operator checklist and gated approvals
A2: Automated validation jobs confirm KV snapshot consistency (sha256) and sequence continuity across promotion window
A3: SLO smoke tests pass for 95th and 99th latency targets within defined RTO in a staged canary traffic window
A4: Circuit-breaker thresholds profiled and default rules committed to runtime config; rollback policy validated
A5: Scheduled drill executed in non-prod and a runbook drill executed in prod with postmortem and run-rate metrics collected
runbook_steps: Step 0: Pre-checks — verify backup snapshot age < configured RPO; ensure monitoring, alerting, and chaos agents disabled for this window
Step 1: Quarantine passive region — mark passive control-plane read-only and redirect non-essential background jobs to maintenance mode
Step 2: KV snapshot & verification — take point-in-time snapshot and run integrity hash; replicate to active region and validate sequence/tombstone counts
Step 3: Incremental drain policy — apply priority-based admission (tier 0 traffic) and enable progressive load shedding for tier 2+ using configured token buckets
Step 4: Circuit-breaker staging — apply conservative open thresholds (latency 95th = baseline * 2.5, error rate 5% absolute) on a small canary domain
Step 5: Promote passive to active (atomic flag flip) — flip routing digest, increment promotion counter, and enable KV write lease with cross-checkers
Step 6: Canary verification (0-5 min) — run synthetic transactions, validate response schemas and token counters, confirm K/V writes surface in snapshots
Step 7: Progressive traffic ramp (5-30 min) — increase traffic to 10%, 30%, 60% subject to SLO gates; if any gate fails, execute rollback plan
Step 8: Full traffic cutover and monitoring stabilization — monitor error budgets, tracing spans for long-tail latency, and landfill queue backlog
Step 9: Post-cutover consistency audit — run end-to-end reconciliation jobs and snapshot verification; if divergence > tolerance, trigger reconciliation workflow
rollback_plan: If any SLO gate fails during canary or ramp, atomically revert routing digest to previous region, re-enable passive region writes in read-only mode, and run incremental patchback to reconcile writes produced during failed promotion. Run incident bridge, notify oncall and PM/Design stakeholders, and schedule a hard-stop until root cause triage completes. Rollback must complete within RTO=15 minutes for critical tenants or trigger emergency eviction of transient traffic using circuit-breakers and priority isolation.
test_plan: 1) Dry-run in staging: full playbook executed with synthetic traffic and simulated partial failures (5% node loss, network blackhole to worker subnets).
2) Backup/Restore validation suite: automated integrity checks (hashes), idempotency tests for replayed writes, and simulated tombstone reconciliation testcases.
3) SLO smoke harness: run 1,000 synthetic requests per second across typical prompt distributions and assert p95/p99 latency and error-rate thresholds under promotion conditions.
4) Circuit-breaker fuzzing: inject controlled latency and error spikes to validate open/half-open transitions and automated backoff behavior.
5) Observability checks: traces, logs, and dashboards updated; alerts tuned to avoid noisy false positives during drills.
